name: Tank Yard v2.1.0
body:
# Tank Yard v2.1.0

Harder boss fights, animated health bars, new recorded sound mixes and a rare encounter beneath the arena. Everything in [v2.0.5](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/releases/v2.0.5.md) is included.

**Multiplayer uses protocol 35. Update the host and all players together.** Clients and servers from 2.0 cannot play with 2.1.0. Existing settings, maps, Luau scripts and signed staff packs carry over.

## Boss fights

- Bosses choose between three special attacks according to range, nearby tanks and their target's movement. Each kind has its own priorities, remembers recent attackers and avoids piling onto the same player as every other boss.
- Later phases increase the pressure and shorten openings. Dangerous attacks still have visible warnings, and cover, sharp turns and defensive abilities remain useful.
- Railgunner's cannon and beam require a parry within **75 milliseconds** of pressing the ability while facing the incoming shot, within about **49 degrees**. Its smaller guns keep the normal parry window.
- Rail, plasma, burning shells and steel slugs have distinct clash effects and sounds. The rail clash has a heavier impact.

## Health bars and effects

- Boss health bars blend their colors smoothly, animate incoming damage and leave a glowing white damage trail. A red outline pulses and glows when the boss targets you.
- The headline bar keeps health, phase markers and attack messages visible while the boss moves off screen. Reduced Motion keeps the health information without the decorative flashes and shake.
- Projectile ribbons use finer curves near the camera. Engine exhaust holds its direction through stops and turns.
- Boss arrivals, weapons, parries, rifts and map sound cues use new mixes of recorded metal, stone, steam and creature performances. The recordings are CC0; credits and source details are in the [sound bank reference](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/assets/audio/foley/README.md).

<details>
<summary>Secret encounter: Sunderworm</summary>

Sunderworm is a long, segmented boss with a ground-shaking entrance. Cracks spread before it breaks through the floor, throwing tiles, earth and dust into the air. Its body can be hit only where it is above ground.

- Five phases introduce lunges, bone fans, bile, burrowing, larvae and spine waves. Watch the strike lane and eruption ring before moving in.
- At **16% health**, it tears into a head and tail that fight independently. A surviving half becomes more aggressive. Both must be destroyed.
- Its jaws unfold around hooked teeth, with a contracting throat and saliva strands. Blood streams break into falling droplets, pool on the floor and dry. Torn flesh, debris and blood use the arena's effects and lighting.
- Its health bar shows phase boundaries and warnings before lunges, eruptions and the split. A half's destruction is distinguished from the end of the encounter.
- An eligible natural boss arrival has about a **one-in-two-million** chance of being Sunderworm and needs an arena worth three full-level tanks. The Boss Rush roster rolls a **one-in-24,000** chance when opened. A selected encounter stays in the saved lineup.
- Hosts can explicitly choose `sunderworm` in a Boss Rush lineup or a map Boss trigger. Presentation packs can keep its local roster card available with `"menu": { "bosses": ["sunderworm"] }`.

</details>

## Stability and performance

- Players joining or reconnecting during a worm fight receive its real body positions. Visible segments and collision shapes stay together, and DLSS motion follows each segment's silhouette.
- Bots aim at nearby surfaced body segments and avoid them even when the head is far away.
- A large finishing hit no longer skips the worm's death effects. Exploding rounds cannot trigger their owner's death scene.
- Destroying both halves in the same tick fires encounter-completion logic and the Boss Rush team bonus once. Whole worms reserve room for their tails within the encounter limit.
- Blood, debris and sound queues have fixed limits. Sounds are prepared and cached for playback, and clients receive body positions without the host's full movement history or decision state.

## Updating a server

Install the **2.1.0 server and client together**, along with any separately deployed relay. Protocol 35 is incompatible with protocol 34 from 2.0.0–2.0.5; the connection screen explains which side needs an update.

See [hosting](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/hosting.md), [Pi and Docker upgrades](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/central-pi-upgrade.md), [bosses](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/bosses-and-learning.md) and [modding](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.1.0/docs/modding.md).

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.0.5
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.0.5

A new boss that would prefer you stayed far away, parries that hit back, and a boss bar that finally looks like part of the game.

## Railgunner

- The biggest regular boss, with a lot of health and a heavier cannon than Siege Engine's. It leads moving targets, hunts whoever is furthest away, and is at its worst when you're right under the barrel.
- Its barrel is the warning. A rail shot only strains the latches. When the plasma beam is coming, the armor splits, the coils spread and the muzzle claws unfold, and the whole thing throws open as its aim locks.
- The beam sweeps after its target, then the boss vents with its barrel still open and takes 40% more damage. That's your window.
- It hops backward when crowded and keeps weak flak guns for anyone who gets close.
- It turns up very rarely on its own, and only in arenas with enough experienced players. You can also pick it in a custom Boss Rush, summon it as staff, or practice in **Get under the rail**.

## Parries that hit back

- Parry the beam and it breaks. The stream stops, a bright clash goes off at your tank, and the strike runs back up the line for 10% of the boss's full health.
- Railgunner's cannon goes back as an ion strike (9%), Siege Engine's shell as fire and a blast (7%), and Bastion's slug as a smaller steel-blue hit (4%). Railgunner's lighter echo round is worth half a cannon clash.
- Each clash has its own look, sound and light. One volley can only clash once, and bots deal 40% of what a player does.
- Reduced motion and Effects at zero keep the headline and damage number without the flashes, particles or camera shake. Attack warnings stay visible.

## Boss effects

- Trails behave like gas left hanging in the air. They stay where they were laid, drift on the wind and spread out as they fade, rather than following the round around like a sticker.
- Bosses leave engine exhaust from where their engines actually are.
- Fire no longer shows faint stripes, and the flame stream holds together in flight.
- The plasma beam curves where it bends instead of folding at the joints.
- The boss bar and the **BOSS INCOMING** and **BOSS DEFEATED** banners are redrawn. The bar shows what the boss is doing, and turns red when it's after you.

## Arena Workshop

- Twenty particle presets, including Flame, Steam, Bubbles, Confetti, Leaves, Ash, Magic, Energy, Blizzard and Pollen. The inspector previews the effect, highlights its preset and shows how many particles are alive.
- Smooth particle sprites at four sizes, feathered rings, motion-stretched sparks, soft light and hot cores. Colors blend through natural intermediate shades. Reduced motion keeps its still preview and disables map particles during play.
- Sixteen widget looks, including Blueprint, Graphite, Signal and Rose. **Copy look** and **Paste look** share a design without replacing text, choices, board cells or logic.
- Widget drawing reuses mesh storage. Inspector previews stop drawing while scrolled out of view.
- Random signals can avoid the previous pick, shuffle every channel once, or pick by weight. Weight bars show each channel's chance; a trigger can send several distinct picks.
- Chance conditions roll a percentage when the trigger attempts to act, including percentages read from counters.
- Twenty more sound presets, with pitch, variation, repeats, timing and Near, Far, Everywhere or Cause audiences. **Hear it** previews the configured cue. Repeated sounds leave room for newly triggered cues.
- Ready-made loot-table, shuffle, pickup and countdown pieces demonstrate the new controls. The [editor guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.5/docs/map-editor.md) covers every setting.

## Staff tools and fixes

- Server staff get a searchable player list, masked ban review and lifting, live server health, and boss summon and dismiss controls. Every action uses the server's existing permissions.
- Lifting a ban restores the address ban if its linked account record can't be saved. Reading server health doesn't fill the audit log.
- Creator tools add boss-health presets, heal-all and jumping beside a living player. Reason and duration presets, unmute and clearer player details improve moderation.
- Fixed the Mods row switch losing its click to the row beneath it. The detail button still works.
- Fixed Unlock becoming unclickable after focusing the password field. Show/Hide and keypad Enter work there too.

Signed staff packs stay portable. Existing packs unlock the updated client, and their passwords and identities don't change.

## Security

- Private server passwords can only be guessed a limited number of times per address, with more room for shared relay addresses.
- One address can no longer fill the party relay's rooms or a WebSocket relay's connections and lock everyone else out.
- Names and chat can't be made of invisible characters, so nobody turns up as a blank on the leaderboard or as a perfect copy of someone else's name.

## Compatibility

This release stays on **protocol 34**, so 2.0 clients and servers keep playing together.

- Railgunner, clashes and the new staff tools come from the server, which needs to run 2.0.5 to have them.
- A 2.0.4 client on a 2.0.5 server sees Railgunner as a very large Siege Engine and a clash as an ordinary parry. Clients older than 2.0.4 still have the boss-timer disconnect that release fixed, so they should update.
- A saved map that names Railgunner needs a 2.0.5 host.

New map logic and sound settings need a 2.0.5 host. Older clients hear a classic fallback for the new sounds. Existing map packs, Luau scripts, settings and staff packs carry over. See [playing](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.5/docs/playing.md), [staff administration](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.5/docs/creator-administration.md) and [server upgrades](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.5/docs/central-pi-upgrade.md).

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.0.4
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.0.4

Fixes boss party disconnects, with smoother boss fire, configurable Boss Rush lineups, and saved maps for parties and offline games.

Boss fire bends along its flight path, Boss Rush lets you choose the lineup, and parties can play your saved maps and switch maps between rounds.

## Boss party disconnect fix

- Fixed clients disconnecting with **"invalid snapshot values"** when a boss has a special ready and briefly waits to turn toward a player. This could happen with Fallen Overlord and other bosses in online matches, including parties.
- Fixed the same disconnect during Siege Engine's and Bastion's longer special-attack warnings.
- Snapshot checks now use the simulation's aim-hold limit and each boss's actual warning duration. Invalid, infinite and NaN timer values are still rejected.
- Added regressions for both friends staying connected, every boss's timer boundaries, and moving two-player fights through all three phases of all fourteen bosses.

This bug was also present in v2.0.3. **Every player should update their client** to receive the fix, including when joining an older host.

## Boss effects

- Trails follow the path each round has flown, smoothing ordinary turns while keeping sharp bounces against walls. Their ends taper and fade smoothly as a round slows or disappears.
- Heavy cannon rounds gain twisting light and flame that move with their trails.
- Soft glows have smoother color transitions on both light and dark floors.
- Tanks hide the light beneath them, including along long or offset barrels. The light mask reuses their drawn geometry, and skips work when there is nothing to hide.
- Corrected visibility and overlap checks at ribbon bends, polygon rims and the screen edge.

## Your Boss Rush

- **Classic six**, **Quick three**, or **Full rush** with all fourteen bosses.
- Choose individual bosses, change their order, adjust the count, or shuffle the lineup. Your choice is saved for later games.
- The round banner shows the current wave, boss and total, and announces who comes next.
- Long lineups reach the same final difficulty increase as the classic six. Shorter lineups keep the usual 14% increase per wave.
- A boss that has nowhere safe to spawn waits for room. If the space stays blocked, the round ends in a draw instead of getting stuck or skipping a boss.

Dedicated servers can set `boss_rush = ["prism", "siege_engine", "trapper"]` above the first TOML section, use `--boss-rush all`, or change the next round through the `boss-rush` console command. See [playing](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.4/docs/playing.md#boss-rush) and [hosting](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.4/docs/hosting.md).

## Party and map choices

- **Change map…** offers built-in arenas, saved Arena Workshop maps and map packs before creating a party or starting its next round.
- Party guests receive the selected map automatically, including when they join later. Existing invites and connections survive a map change.
- The leader's chosen Boss Rush lineup applies to the party.
- Map packs are prepared asynchronously so the client can keep handling menus and networking while it waits. Invalid settings or packs leave the current round intact.
- Saved maps chosen from the same picker also launch correctly in offline play.

See [parties](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.4/docs/parties.md).

## Compatibility and validation

This release keeps **protocol 34**, compatible with other 2.0 clients and servers. Custom Boss Rush lineups and party map changes require a host running 2.0.4; the visual improvements run in the client. Existing maps, packs and settings carry over.

Before release, 988 Rust tests passed with four existing hardware or environment tests ignored. Formatting, strict Clippy, installer tests, content checks, the optimized workspace build and Windows/macOS compilation checks passed. Linux visual checks covered light and dark themes, enlarged menus, live party map switching and all sixteen game modes. Windows and macOS runtime verification is performed by the release workflow's installation checks.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.0.3
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.0.3

The bosses have started paying attention, Axiom finally has a body worth being afraid of, and the scoreboard folds up when you're tired of seeing who's beating you. It plays with 2.0.0 and 2.0.2, so nobody has to update at the same time.

## Bosses

- **They aim now.** Bosses lead a moving tank and, just before a special, line up on where you'll be when the warning ends. A sharp turn can still slip the shot, so dodging remains a valid career.
- **Straight lines.** They drive in clean legs from one heading to the next, closing in, backing off or cutting around you, instead of drifting about.
- **They notice when you're hurt.** A wounded tank is a more attractive target than it used to be. Sorry.
- **Bastion has a cannon.** Same hull, one heavy round with a proper warning. It's lighter than the Siege Engine's, so it ruins your day rather than ending it. Once Bastion is badly hurt, explosive charges bracket the line.
- A few bosses got small buffs, mostly quicker and meaner drones.

See [Bosses and learning](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.3/docs/bosses-and-learning.md).

## Axiom Worldshaper

- Rebuilt from the hull up on the glow engine: six working cannons, a turning gold and teal astrolabe, and attacks that look like they cost something.
- All twelve attacks sit on a dock with number keys, cooldowns and tooltips.
- Holding fire walks a stream of shells across the forward cannons, and they meet at your cursor.

## Scoreboard, party and chat

- **An arrow folds the scoreboard away,** and **L** does the same. It stays how you left it.
- **Each row shows that player's tank,** in miniature, so you know what's about to happen to you.
- With the tank menu open the board shortens to clear it, and your own row stays on it however the match is going.
- **Party rows show whose mic is off.** The silence now comes with an explanation.
- **Up and Down in chat** bring back what you already said, in case it was worth saying twice.

## Arena Workshop

- **Ctrl+F finds things** by kind, group, number or what a trigger does, and steps through the results.
- Drawing, moving and resizing show live measurements, and the status bar gives the size of your selection.
- Undo and redo say what they changed and flash it on the map.
- The Check list keeps itself up to date while you work.
- Copying with nothing selected no longer empties your clipboard. It was a very efficient way to lose a clipboard.

See [the map editor guide](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.3/docs/map-editor.md).

## Installing and speed

- The shell installer for Linux, macOS and FreeBSD now unpacks in your cache folder rather than `/tmp`, so a small or full temporary drive no longer stops an install. If extraction still fails, your current game is left alone.
- A busy match makes about a fifth fewer memory allocations per frame. The picture is the same.

## Compatibility

Tank Yard 2.0.3 still uses **protocol 34**, so it plays with 2.0.0 and 2.0.2 clients and servers, and maps and packs carry over unchanged. Boss behavior and Axiom's cannons come from the server, so you'll see them offline and on servers running 2.0.3.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.0.2
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.0.2

Everything that glows got a second look, the Siege Engine's shell is now properly on fire, and your party can finally hear you complain from the other side of the map. It plays with 2.0.0, so nobody has to update at the same moment.

## Bosses

- **Better fireworks.** Shots, muzzle flashes, hull lights, warnings and explosions on all fourteen bosses are redrawn with the game's glow lighting, and they stay bright on dark maps.
- **The Siege Engine's round is on fire.** It burns the whole way there, drags a flame trail behind it and leaves a scorch mark where you used to be.
- **Smoother movement.** Bosses ease through turns, sidestep your shots without twitching and steer around walls instead of grinding along them. Fights last about as long as they did.
- **Health bars you can read.** Notches mark where the next phase starts, and a pale stretch shows the damage you just did.
- **Arrows to bosses off screen,** with their names and health, so you can find the fight again after a respawn. Or avoid it. Nobody's judging.
- **Parting words.** Every boss now has something to say on your death screen. None of it is nice.

## Party voice

- Everyone in a party hears each other at full volume, anywhere: across the arena, while down, in a menu or between rounds.
- A mute button with the usual microphone icon is on the party rail, in the party panel and in the match, and **M** still works. Your mic starts muted, so nobody hears you eating.
- A ring around a member's tank shows who's talking. Muting someone only mutes them for you, and they never need to find out.
- The party's leader needs 2.0.2 for this. With a 2.0.0 leader, voice works by distance as before.

See [Voice](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.2/docs/parties.md#voice).

## Arena Workshop

- **A Links view you can actually follow.** Busy channels gather at hubs, wires heading the same way run together as cables, and a key in the corner hides or shows each kind of link. Point at a hub to lift its wires out of the spaghetti.
- **Gates look like gates.** Every piece in the Gates and Circuits palettes has its own symbol.
- **Connections.** The inspector lists what a trigger sets off and what sets it off. Click a row to go there.
- **Clicks take the smallest thing under the pointer,** so a trigger sitting on a spawn region no longer needs a rescue mission.
- The layer bar opens a strip of every layer in use, and just selecting something no longer marks your map as edited.

## Graphics and speed

- **NVIDIA DLAA** has its own button in Graphics.
- A typical match now takes about half the draw calls and a twentieth of the memory allocations per frame. The picture is exactly the same, which was the point.

## Compatibility

Tank Yard 2.0.2 still uses **protocol 34**, so it plays with 2.0.0 clients and servers, and maps and packs carry over unchanged.

earlier.name: Tank Yard v2.0.0
earlier.body:
# Tank Yard v2.0.0

The biggest update Tank Yard has had. All fourteen bosses are redrawn and fight harder, tanks are rebuilt and rebalanced, the Arena Workshop gains layers, map logic gains real gates and circuits, and parties are much better to play in. Everything in [v1.7.0](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/releases/v1.7.0.md) is included.

## Bosses

- **New looks.** Every boss is redrawn in clean, simple shapes, each with a glowing core that brightens as it charges and pulses when it's nearly beaten.
- **Attacks you can read.** Before a special attack, a boss shows where its rounds will go: lanes for a fan, spokes for a ring and chevrons for a charge. Lances, darts, shells and charges each have their own look and glow.
- **The Siege Engine's cannon.** It winds up for 1.5 seconds and draws a red line to the first wall in its way, then fires a huge, very fast round that destroys any tank it reaches, shields included. Get off the line or behind cover. Walls stop it, spawn protection holds, and a perfect parry sends it back as a heavy shot.
- **Fights that fit the arena.** A boss's health follows how many players are in the arena and how high their levels are. It moves with them if they join or leave, keeping how hurt the boss is. Bosses with swarms launch fewer drones against fewer players, and reach their full swarm against four.
- **Shared rewards.** Everyone who hit a boss in the last minute shares its reward.
- **Smarter help.** High-level bots now join a boss fight while they're healthy enough for it, and shoot down the drones that chase them.
- A warned attack always comes, even if its target ducks behind cover.

See [Fighting bosses in 2.0](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/bosses-and-learning.md#fighting-bosses-in-20).

## Tanks

- **21 new layouts.** Bastion, Catapult, Commodore, Cyclone Gunner, Drone Sentinel, Fabricator, Fortress Array, Gunship, Interceptor, Javelin, Monolith, Octo Sprayer, Palisade, Pinball, Quarry, Railstorm, Rotator, Spectral Guard, Starburst, Switchback and Tri-Sniper have cleaner, balanced shapes, with turrets on proper mounts.
- **Rebalanced from thousands of bot duels.** 65 tanks changed.
- **The strongest came down.** Reprisal and Railstorm deal about half the damage they did, and both fire more slowly. Reprisal also has less health and a longer ability cooldown. Mirage lost 19%, and Ranger, Capacitor, Overcharger, Catapult, Riposte, Counterguard, Sniper, Stalker and others lost up to 15%.
- **The weakest came up.** Rook, Pinball and Bastille, the weakest level-55 tanks, gained 26 to 33%: Bastille lays traps faster and Rook places turrets sooner. Machine Gun gained 15%, and Destroyer, Annihilator, Spread Shot, Fighter, Triple Shot, Octo Tank, Tri-Angle and others gained up to 9%.

## Arena Workshop

- **Layers.** Every object sits on a layer from 0 to 99. The layer bar and the **,** and **.** keys pick a layer (hold Shift to skip empty ones). Everything else fades and can't be selected, so you can reach what's underneath. Layers are only for building and never change how a map plays.
- **Reach what's stacked.** Clicking the one selected object again selects the next object under the pointer, top to bottom, and wraps round.
- **The Links view (L) shows every connection.** Busy channels and counters gather at a hub so a large circuit stays readable, and drawing it is much cheaper on low-end computers.

See [Layers](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/map-editor.md#layers).

## Map logic

- **More gates.** Alongside All, Any, Not all, None and One, a gate can now open on an even number of true conditions (XNOR, or NOT with one condition), an odd number (parity) or most of them (majority). A trigger can check eight conditions, up from four.
- **Live gates.** **On input change** runs a trigger whenever a counter or group its conditions read changes, and **Gate to counter** writes the gate's result to a counter. Together they make gates that follow their inputs, and a chain of them settles within a tick.
- **A Circuits palette.** Ready-made live gates, sum and carry bits, latches, comparators, registers, numbers and pulses. The Gates palette adds NOT, NAND, NOR, XNOR, majority and parity.
- **Faster and larger.** **Every** can run as often as every 0.05 seconds. Each tick allows 32,768 chained actions and 262,144 condition checks, and 16,384 delayed actions can wait at once. Boards follow counters within two ticks.

See [Live gates](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/map-editor.md#live-gates).

## Parties

- The party rail shows each member's health, turns grey when they're down, and says when someone joins or leaves.
- On a team, arrows at the edge of the screen point toward allies out of view, with their names.
- The party panel lists each member's level, what they're doing, their tank and their health.
- The leader can remove a member with **Kick**, confirmed with a second click.

See [In a match](https://github.com/RobertFlexx/tankyard/blob/v2.0.0/docs/parties.md#in-a-match).

## Gatewright

- An opponent's rifts now look different from yours: crimson and amber, ringed with thorns. Your own side's stay violet and teal.
- Rounds glide through rifts instead of jumping or streaking across the arena.

## Fixes

- Clicks no longer pass through one panel to what's under it. Clicking a tank upgrade over the party icon, for example, now only picks the upgrade.
- Co-op boss waves are tougher, and grow more with the size of the party.
- A window now always draws at its own size, so it stays sharp when maximized and runs faster when it's smaller than the chosen resolution. Resolution still sets the render size in fullscreen, and Render scale works in both.

## Compatibility

Tank Yard 2.0.0 uses **protocol 34**. Update clients, servers and separate relays together; 1.7.0 uses protocol 33. Older maps and packs still open. Maps that use the new gates, more than four conditions, On input change, Gate to counter or timers under 0.25 seconds need 2.0.0.
